title: Beef, round, eye of round roast, boneless, separable lean only, trimmed to 0" fat, select, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Eye of round roast is a lean cut taken from the rear leg of the cow. The product is boneless, contains only the separable lean portion, and is trimmed to zero visible fat. It is a select grade piece commonly used for roasting, grilling, or making steaks. Raw beef is a rich source of protein, iron, zinc, and B‑vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eye of round is one of the leanest beef cuts, typically containing less than 5 % fat.
It is often used in dishes that require slow, low‑heat cooking to keep the meat tender.
Boneless cuts cook faster and are easier to slice than bone‑in equivalents.
The name comes from the eye‑shaped appearance of the muscle.
In the United States this cut is frequently labeled “select,” indicating a moderate level of marbling.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 22 g of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and riboflavin (B2), supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: The trimmed lean portion fits well into low‑fat dietary plans while still delivering nutrients.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Raw beef may harbor pathogenic bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella). Cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: Excess intake can aggravate gout in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rare, but some people may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Sodium in processed versions
items.content: If the product is pre‑salted, consider total sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The eye of round can be roasted at 180 °C for 20‑30 minutes, grilled, or quickly pan‑seared. Marinating in an acidic medium (lemon juice, vinegar) or using a low‑and‑slow cooking method helps keep it tender. Slice across the grain for maximum tenderness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container for 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C in a vacuum‑sealed bag for up to 6 months. Thaw in the fridge before use, never at room temperature.
